patch.title: Athos I and II: 450 MW Solar Operating Since 2022
patch.description: California State Lands Commission’s October 2024 staff report describes two fully operating Athos solar facilities totaling 450 MW. EIA identifies Athos I at 250 MW, operating June 2022, and Athos II at 200 MW, operating December 2021. A later CEC filing says solar construction was completed in July 2022.

references.title: California State Lands Commission — October 17, 2024 Staff Report 50
CEC October 8, 2025 backup materials — Athos storage environmental addendum
EIA August 2026 Inventory — Athos I 63300 and Athos II 64290
SB Energy — Energy Projects / Athos
CAISO Public Queue — Athos Power Plant 1405

patch.longFormSummary:
• Native 450 MW is solar-only combined AC nameplate, not 450 MWdc and not additive battery export. EIA’s generator operating months differ from July 2022 overall solar-construction completion. Separate Athos storage is not represented as already operating; CAISO’s 2027 proposed completion covers a hybrid request, not proof the existing solar is still proposed.
  • The CEC materials describe the original 3,440-acre project envelope, a 3,224-acre solar footprint and separate approximately 31-acre BESS proposal. Those scopes are not silently equated to the former 3,400-acre claim. No opened $500M capital-cost evidence or May 18, 2022 COD; the BLM ePlanning landing page does not establish either.
  • Timeline: July 1 is a month-only placeholder for July 2022 solar-construction completion stated in CEC materials, not an exact COD. EIA separately reports December 2021 / June 2022 operating months for II / I.
  • Historical Athos I construction image from the operator project page; not the entire combined Athos I/II project or completed battery. Credit: SB Energy.
  • Operator Athos solar-plant image with sheep; not a battery system or proof of a precise operating day. Credit: SB Energy.
  • The State Lands Commission names SE Athos I, LLC and SE Athos II, LLC; SB Energy presents Athos in its current portfolio. Separate storage is not part of the solar MW.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: July 1 is a month-only placeholder for July 2022 solar-construction completion stated in CEC materials, not an exact COD. EIA separately reports December 2021 / June 2022 operating months for II / I.
patch.company: SE Athos I, LLC and SE Athos II, LLC
patch.address: EIA shared Athos I/II reporting point near Desert Center, Riverside County, California; not a surveyed solar or battery boundary

power.note: Athos I 250 MW + Athos II 200 MW EIA operating AC solar nameplate. Separate battery omitted; not 450 MWdc or measured output.

gaps: Verify precise project-wide completion day and built solar boundary; EIA operating months and overall construction completion are different milestones. Operator Athos I legacy page still says under construction; regulator and EIA operating evidence controls.

patch.title: Grand Junction / Karma J1313: 100 MW Solar Development
patch.description: MISO J1313 identifies a 100 MW solar request in Greene County at the Karma 161 kV bus, with post-GIA status Not Started and a stale June 30, 2025 negotiated target. The IUB’s April 21, 2023 release describes Grand Junction Solar at the same substation; later county-meeting reporting identifies Alliant as the purchaser.

• The IUB release supports a conditional certificate for up to 100 MW solar plus a separate 50 MW battery in the original 1,103-acre project area; it is not evidence of construction or current battery installation. Native 100 MW is solar only. MISO’s old negotiated target is not realized COD.
  • Alliant’s April 2024 county update is corroborated by the official agenda and meeting report; the latter says it purchased the project from National Grid Renewables. A 2026 report quotes prospective 2027/2028 construction and a possible future battery amendment; that is not a 2027 operating deadline or approved 100 MW battery. Its August 14 publication label refers to an August 17 meeting, so no precise 2026 event date is adopted.
  • Removed $130M, fabricated Karma Clean Solar Center branding and stale Geronimo-only ownership. The retained approximate location is county/project-area context, not a surveyed solar parcel or exact substation point.
  • Timeline: Confirmed April 21, 2023 conditional certificate milestone in the IUB’s republished release; not COD. The original order link currently returns a filing portal rather than downloadable order.

researchNotes: Nine existing pins corrected and three soft-deleted/held on local and production. Initial title/source/author identities matched across environments; stale local IDs reconciled before writing. Re-read immediately before each mutation, preserved original authors, saved backups and synchronized draft/held catalogs and posted maps. No new pins or automatic merges.

Read the primary August 2026 EIA inventory, September 2026 ERCOT GIS workbook, CAISO queue and freshly downloaded MISO live GI JSON. Stored matching rows and complete primary filings. Queue dates, proposed ratings, generator AC capacity, gross-terminal ratings, battery MWh and actual operation are distinct.

Athos: State Lands Commission October 2024 Staff Report 50 supports two operating solar facilities totaling 450 MW. EIA separates I / 63300 / 250 MW / June 2022 and II / 64290 / 200 MW / December 2021. CEC October 2025 materials say overall solar construction completed July 2022. Saved July 1 as explicit month-only construction-completion placeholder, not an exact COD. The old May 18, 2022 day and $500M lack support. The original 3,440-acre envelope, 3,224-acre solar footprint and separate 31-acre proposed BESS are not one interchangeable acreage. CAISO 1405 hybrid timing in 2027 does not override operating solar evidence. Legacy SB Athos I page still says under construction; regulator/EIA evidence controls. Company resolver maps SB Energy to SoftBank Group, so use the regulator-named project entities and retain SB attribution in cited text. No shared company row edited.

18-Alpha / 28INR0328: 307.4 MW, Cooke County, SCOUT ENERGY MANAGEMENT LLC, Valley View 138 kV bus 691, February 1, 2028 projected COD. 18-Bravo / 28INR0327: 407 MW, Hunt County, same legal applicant, Commerce Switch 138 kV bus 1816 and same target. Both show screening complete, full study started, no IA. Removed misidentified Energy Management Inc., $300M / $400M and invented 1,230 / 1,628 MWh four-hour claims. No exact-name EIA match or verified branch-specific gallery found.

Agricola / 28INR0265: 205.2 MW, Austin County, Agricola BESS LLC, Gebhardt–Wallis 138 kV tap, May 31, 2029 target, screening completed and study started without IA. No opened primary support for Redeux parent, construction, $200M, 821 MWh or four-hour duration. The New York Agricola Wind EIA entry is unrelated. No verified exact project photograph or parcel located.

Anila 16770 held as duplicate of Alina battery 16675. Full May 19, 2025 PUCT filing names Alina Energy LLC / Alina Solar and BESS with requests 26INR0074 and 26INR0077; technical exhibit also calls it Anila. The signed agreement dates to March 2025. It specifies 200 MW battery at POI, 211.14792 MW gross inverter terminals and separate 200 MW solar; ERCOT reports 209 MW. These are rating differences, not a new battery identity or proof of 836 MWh. Retained 16675 has the operator 200 MW / 400 MWh battery and EIA 67250. Preserved it unchanged and did not silently add the new filing to another pin.

IAD02: operator December 4, 2020 blog records December 3 topping out. Published two-story 513,000 sqft, expandable 120 MW, shared 26-acre campus and current address 21821 Uunet Drive. Native rating is explicitly expandable design, not energized or measured load. Corrected 163.1 MW modeled demand / 116.5 MW IT, $4.43B, 624,570 sqft, 122 acres and June 2023 COD. Indexed 2021 sheet lists both 513,000 headline sqft and 438,460 building sqft but the actual PDF returns 404 from old and new paths; keep opened announcement/case-study historical 513,000 scope with the discrepancy recorded. Original DEQ retrieval returns 403, not proof the facility is unsupported. Six current building photos and a historical topping-out photo retained.

IAD03: July 26, 2022 release dateline controls over July 25 metadata. It announces a ten-acre Sterling campus master-planned for two buildings and then-targeted fall-2023 phase-one delivery. Current address 22715 Relocation Drive replaces Beaumeade Circle. Current market page repeats 26-acre text for IAD03, conflicting with announced ten-acre scope; save ten acres as historical and flag current land scope unresolved. No published current IT MW, gross area or COD supports old 143.1 / 102.2 MW, 319,384 sqft, $3.88B and January 2025 claims. Native power deleted. One current operator aerial and one explicitly labeled 2022 proposed-building rendering added.

NEO-03 16783 held as unverified building-level split. Downloaded and read the 17.4 MB December 27, 2024 Ohio EPA PTI P0137086, facility 0322022037, named Aligned NE001 Sandusky at 2509 Hayes Avenue: 186 emergency generators across permitted scope. It does not establish a separately rated 82.8 MW / 72 MW IT third building or June 2029 COD. NEO-01 16724 and the wider expansion 15776 already represent the site. Permit names and proposed backup scope do not validate each tracker building. Retained counterparts unchanged; their old tracker expansion ratings remain a dedicated follow-up, not validated by this hold.

Northwest Point Building 2 / 16787 held as redundant/unverified split of retained ORD-03 campus 15743. The downloaded June 21, 2024 IEPA notification is an application-under-review letter for 112 emergency generator sets at 50 and 150 NW Point Blvd, not a final permit or an individual 110.4 MW building rating. Official village 2024 review supports two buildings and $285M campus investment; March 2025 newsletter records January 14 first-building topping out. The newsletter contains an obvious 520 million sqft typo, so it was not used to assign floor area. Neither source establishes this split’s independent identity, June 2029 COD or building-only cost. The wider campus pin’s tracker-derived MW needs a later audit.

Karma J1313: MISO 100 MW solar / Greene / ITC Midwest / GIA completed January 26, 2023 / post-GIA Not Started / negotiated June 30, 2025. The IUB’s April 21, 2023 press release, republished by KWBG and linked to original docket/order, supports a conditional certificate for Grand Junction 100 MW solar plus separate original 50 MW battery at Karma, not actual construction. Original order now serves filing-portal HTML. April 2024 official county agenda and firsthand meeting reporting identify Alliant’s project update; the report says Alliant purchased it from National Grid Renewables. August 2026 reporting describes future 2027/2028 construction and a possible battery amendment, not an approved new 100 MW battery or 2027 COD. Its publication/meeting-date anomaly is explicit. Saved the verified April 2023 certificate milestone, cleared $130M and invented Karma branding, and retained a qualified approximate point. Direct newspaper requests return 406 while web-open retrieval succeeds; county agenda is web-indexed but direct requests return 403.

Flora / J1679: opened MTEP23 explicitly names New Fauna 345 kV Sub for Flora Solar and ties 125 MW to J1679 / Xenia–Mount Vernon West. EIA 67937 reports Flora Solar LLC, 125 MW, approvals not initiated, December 2027. MISO post-GIA Not Started and old April 20, 2026 negotiated date do not prove operation. EIA says PJM balancing authority despite MISO identity; that mismatch remains unresolved. Replaced invented Xenia branding, $160M and April 1, 2027 date. The $11M MTEP substation item is not total solar capex. Historical Apex site is migrating: homepage Coming Soon, about_flora redirects to inaccessible migration page. No stock photo or current ownership inference adopted.

Adams / J1072: live MISO confirms 150 MW solar, Mower County, Northern States Power Company transmission owner, GIA completion June 15, 2021 and post-GIA Under Construction, with stale August 1, 2023 negotiated target. Saved dated GIA queue milestone; no actual COD inferred. Cleared $190M, invented Adams branding, ITC Midwest attribution, December 2026 and unverified NextEra ownership. Mower County’s [February 14, 2023 minutes](https://co.mower.mn.us/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_02142023-390), opened through web PDF retrieval but returning 404 to a direct request, discuss NextEra’s later 100 MW Timberwolf proposal. This was not silently equated to J1072 or asserted as its developer in the saved pin; exact mapping remains a gap. No confirmed exact-name EIA match or project gallery.

Cleared nine unsupported prices and two calculated energy rows per environment. Replaced both retained data-center metric rows to remove unsupported daily water, installed hardware and generator figures. IAD03 native power removed; IAD02 uses qualified 120 MW expansion design. Held records are no longer public and are not claimed as cancelled.

Four location corrections required twelve replacement USGS maps: current Census street-address contexts for IAD02/IAD03 and EIA reporting points for Athos/Flora. These are qualified context, not surveyed footprints; basemaps can predate construction. The five remaining retained records keep fifteen legacy maps. No precise parcel inferred from county coordinates.

Added eleven credited gallery assets after visual inspection: ten operator photographs (six IAD02 current-building, one IAD02 topping-out, one IAD03 aerial, historical Athos I construction and Athos solar grazing) and one 2022 IAD03 rendering. The IAD02 image labeled Exterior by operator alt text actually shows an interior lounge and is captioned accurately. Excluded the dark Athos crew image, Athos Storage thumbnail, generic stock, other-building galleries and unsupported project imagery. All eleven passed plain-curl exact-byte comparisons. All 23 new Azure assets were publicly byte-verified before switching references.

Fresh verification covers all 24 environment actions, 38 current Azure files, 18 retained native pages and eight unchanged-counterpart checks across four retained pins on both environments. Both posted maps now contain 1,403 entries. No deployment, restart, production build or application-code changes.
